metadata.title: Oracle Stock Jumps as AI Infrastructure Revenue Soars 121%

content.text:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.
Oracle (ORCL) shares jumped about 4% as the software company raised its full-year revenue forecast and highlighted growing demand for its AI infrastructure.
Oracle reported record first-quarter revenue of $19.3 billion, up 30% from a year earlier. Cloud infrastructure revenue climbed 121% to $7.4 billion, while non-GAAP earnings per share reached $1.92.
The company said it delivered 850 megawatts of AI capacity containing more than 300,000 GPUs to customers since the end of the prior quarter. Oracle also closed more than $30 billion in additional AI contracts during the period without raising additional capital.
For the second quarter, management expects revenue growth of 30% to 34% and adjusted EPS of $1.85 to $1.93. Full-year revenue is now projected at at least $90 billion, while non-GAAP EPS guidance increased to $8.10 from $8.05.
Oracle's AI expansion is requiring heavy investment. Capital expenditures reached $28 billion in the quarter, resulting in negative free cash flow of $5 billion, with full-year spending expected at $90 billion to $95 billion.
